dashboard.title: How the Dashboard works
dashboard.description: The Dashboard gives an overview of the current Wari situation.
steps: Check the current risk and crowd indicators.
Review active alerts that may need attention.
Check available emergency and support resources.
Use Digital Twin and Simulation when you need deeper analysis.
dashboard.note: The Dashboard supports officials by bringing important information together in one place.

alerts.title: How Alerts work
alerts.description: Alerts highlight situations that may require attention.
steps: Check the affected zone.
Review the predicted risk and available information.
Check the recommended response.
Use Resources or Simulation to evaluate the next action.
alerts.note: An alert is a decision-support signal. Officials should verify the situation before taking action.

resources.title: How Resource Management works
resources.description: This section shows available resources and suggested deployments.
steps: Select the resource you want to review.
Check its current location and availability.
Review the suggested destination and estimated time.
Use Test in Simulation to understand the possible impact.
resources.note: Resource recommendations support operational planning. Final deployment remains with the authorized authority.

digitalTwin.title: How Digital Twin works
digitalTwin.description: The Digital Twin provides a visual representation of the operational environment.
steps: Select a zone or route on the map.
Review the current crowd and resource situation.
Observe important operational changes.
Use Simulation when you want to test a possible action.
digitalTwin.note: The Digital Twin represents operational information and simulation data; it does not replace field verification.

simulation.title: How What-If Simulation works
simulation.description: Simulation lets officials compare possible actions before approving them.
steps: Select a situation you want to test.
Run the simulation.
Compare the predicted situation before and after the action.
Review the recommendation and approve or reject the action.
simulation.note: Simulation provides decision support. Final operational decisions remain with authorized human officials.

assistant.title: How the AI Assistant works
assistant.description: The AI Assistant explains information from the VARISETU system in simple language.
steps: Ask a question about risks, resources, routes or simulations.
The system uses available operational information.
The assistant explains the information in an easier-to-understand form.
Use the explanation together with the system data before making a decision.
assistant.note: The AI Assistant explains information and supports decisions. It does not make operational decisions.

help.commonNote: This explanation is designed to help every user understand the feature before using it.

dashboard.title: How does the Command Center work?
dashboard.description: The Command Center gives authorities one place to monitor the Wari situation, understand risks and review recommended actions.
steps: View the current situation through key indicators.
Check active alerts and areas requiring attention.
Review AI-generated recommendations.
Use the Digital Twin and simulation tools to understand possible outcomes.

alerts.title: How do Active Alerts work?
alerts.description: Active Alerts highlight situations that may require attention, such as high crowd risk, heat risk or resource shortages.
steps: The system receives current operational information.
Potentially important situations are identified.
Alerts are shown according to their severity.
Authorities can review the situation and decide what action to take.

resources.title: How does Resource Management work?
resources.description: Resource Management helps authorities understand where available resources are located and where they may be needed.
steps: View available ambulances, volunteers and other resources.
Identify areas with higher requirements.
Review resource assignments.
Authorities can approve or modify the recommended deployment.

digitalTwin.title: How does the Digital Twin work?
digitalTwin.description: The Digital Twin provides a virtual representation of the operational Wari environment, showing zones, routes, crowd conditions, risks and resources.
steps: The virtual environment represents important Wari entities.
Current operational information is shown on the map.
Authorities can examine routes, risks and resources.
What-if scenarios can be used to understand possible outcomes.

simulation.title: How does What-If Simulation work?
simulation.description: Simulation allows an authority to test a possible action before applying it to the real situation.
steps: Select a possible intervention.
The system changes the virtual scenario.
The resulting route and operational changes are calculated.
Before-and-after results can be compared before making a decision.

assistant.title: How does the AI Assistant work?
assistant.description: The AI Assistant explains information and recommendations in simple language so that authorities can understand the situation more easily.
steps: Ask a question in natural language.
The assistant uses available system information.
It explains the relevant prediction or recommendation.
The final operational decision remains with the authorized human.
